name: Bidirectional Mission Control & Human Intervention Command Contract
architecture_invariant: USER ACTION -> VALIDATION -> MISSION GATE -> STATE TRANSITION -> EXECUTION/SCHEDULING -> EVIDENCE -> UI UPDATE

APPROVE.description: Approves or rejects a task paused in PENDING_APPROVAL state, unblocking or cancelling its execution tree.
preconditions: target_task_id exists in mission task graph
target task status must be PENDING_APPROVAL
mission must not be in terminal state (COMPLETED, FAILED, CANCELLED)
postconditions: If approved=true: target task status transitions to READY or RUNNING; next step is dispatched to assigned agent
If approved=false: target task status transitions to FAILED/REJECTED; dependents marked BLOCKED
mission_version increments by 1
Audit ledger records decision with operator user_id and reason

PAUSE.description: Cooperatively suspends active mission execution at nearest safe task boundary.
preconditions: mission status is RUNNING, REPAIRING, or REPLANNING
mission is not already PAUSED or in terminal state
postconditions: Active running task completes checkpoint or yields execution lease
mission status transitions to PAUSED
mission_version increments by 1
Audit ledger records PAUSE event

RESUME.description: Resumes execution of a PAUSED mission from latest durable checkpoint.
postconditions: mission status transitions to RUNNING
Agent scheduler re-activates leases for pending ready tasks
mission_version increments by 1
Audit ledger records RESUME event

CANCEL.description: Irreversibly cancels mission execution, terminating running workers and finalizing evidence.
preconditions: mission is not already in terminal state (COMPLETED, FAILED, CANCELLED)
postconditions: mission status transitions to CANCELLING, then immediately to CANCELLED
All active task leases revoked; running tasks cancelled
Complete execution history, logs, and partial evidence are permanently preserved
mission_version increments by 1
Audit ledger records CANCEL with operator reason

CHANGE_PRIORITY.description: Modifies priority level (CRITICAL, HIGH, NORMAL, LOW) of a target task without violating DAG structure.
preconditions: target_task_id exists in mission task graph
target task is not in terminal status (COMPLETED, FAILED, CANCELLED)
priority value is one of CRITICAL, HIGH, NORMAL, LOW
postconditions: target task priority updated in task record
Scheduler queue dynamically re-sorted by priority for ready tasks
DAG topological dependency constraints remain strictly preserved
mission_version increments by 1
Audit ledger records priority change

REORDER.description: Adjusts task execution order within permissible topological bounds, strictly refusing cycle creation or dependency violations.
preconditions: Adjacent swap target exists in specified direction
Swap does not move target task before any prerequisite/dependency
Swap does not move target task after any task that depends on target task
postconditions: Task sequence order swapped in mission plan
DAG remains acyclic and topographically valid
mission_version increments by 1
Audit ledger records REORDER event

safety_gates.sentinel_security_gate: Every command is evaluated against Security Sentinel before gate dispatch; blocked commands return SECURITY_BLOCK and are logged in audit ledger.
safety_gates.optimistic_concurrency_lock: If expected_mission_version does not match current mission_version, command is rejected with STALE status to prevent lost updates.
safety_gates.idempotency_cache: Duplicate idempotency_key within cache window returns identical cached CommandResult without executing duplicate state transitions.
safety_gates.topological_invariance: Task reordering cannot violate causal dependencies: predecessor cannot be scheduled after successor; cycle formation is strictly prevented.
